comment: Where-to-stay area comparisons per island. stays = link to our curated/area stays page; otherwise falls back to the island stays page in build.js.

oahu.blurb: The classic Honolulu base — beach out front, hundreds of restaurants and shops, and most tours pick up here. Busy and central.
Calm, man-made swimming lagoons on the sunny leeward side. Four Seasons, Aulani and Marriott — great for families, quieter and a drive from Honolulu.
Legendary winter waves, food trucks and turtle beaches. Laid-back and rural — best if you want to escape the city and have a car.
Powder-sand Kailua and Lanikai beaches on the windward side. Mostly vacation rentals, quiet and residential — a car is essential.

maui.blurb: Upscale resorts, golden beaches and calm water on the sunny south shore. Polished, pricey and relaxed.
A long resort beach with the Whalers Village shops and easy snorkeling at Black Rock. Lively and convenient.
Historic harbor town (rebuilding) and the greener, more secluded resorts of Kapalua to the north.
Condos and casual eats along the south shore — the most budget-friendly Maui base, with sunny beaches and sunsets.

kauai.blurb: The south shore's reliably sunny resort area — great beaches, snorkeling and spinner dolphins. The easy all-rounder.
Lush north shore with jaw-dropping cliffs, waterfalls and Hanalei Bay. Stunning, rainier, and the gateway to the Nāpali Coast.
The east 'Coconut Coast' — central to the whole island, more affordable, with easy access to the airport and both shores.

big-island.blurb: The sunny west-coast hub — walkable town, manta ray night dives and calm swimming. Central for most Kona-side tours.
The island's top resorts (Waikoloa, Mauna Kea, Mauna Lani) on black-lava coastline with the best white-sand beaches.
The lush, rainy east side — waterfalls, gardens and the closest base to Hawai'i Volcanoes National Park. Fewer resorts, more local.
